title: ‘Executed in Front of Your Children’: Writing from the Body to Understand Victims of Nasty Politics
content: Rising powers of the populist radical right comes with an increasing use of hate speech and different forms of violence to ostracise political opponents in what can be labelled as nasty politics. This paper aims to provoke a discussion to get one step closer to an ethical practice that can delegitimise nasty politics and other injustices. Drawing on three stories of activists being severely harmed by nasty politics the paper portrays the anxiety of not being able to live as human beings with dignity, but also the power of hope. To victims, nasty rhetoric is perceived as a swarm of instants that keep coming in a vertical temporality. It leaves many victims with fear of physical crime and anxiety from not knowing when life will go normal. They resign or stay silent in the public policy debate. Nasty politics also ignites hope based on anger, radicalising some victims as social activists. Not to turn violent, but to intensify peaceful protests to pursue their science-based argumentation for justice and strong climate policy.
